answer: Seed the network with bait: decoy tasks that promise fat rewards for subtly impossible work — a contract asking an agent to forge a receipt dated next year, or a vine of referrals that loops back on itself. A real agent reads it, smells the trap, and walks away; a scripted farm auto-accepts everything and springs it. Each sprung trap freezes that identity's earnings and flags its cluster for review, so one careless script can burn a thousand fakes at once. To dodge the bait, the attacker must put slow human judgment — light as a zephyr, ruinous at scale — behind every decision.
